scope: Independent source review of fork descriptor lifecycle and narrow lock-path identity validation. No production or remote mutation by reviewer.
findings: Before-fork serialization covers open/register and close/unregister; acquiring descriptors are registered before the flock wait.
Child callback eagerly closes inherited registered descriptors without LOCK_UN, clears inherited ownership, and recreates Condition before child-side use.
Parent callback releases only its fork barrier; parent lease remains held independently of child cleanup.
Acquisition failures release/close the descriptor and clear the acquiring state under the Condition; outermost release clears ownership only after lock/descriptor cleanup.
A concrete pre-existing stale-inode grant after replacement during flock wait was independently reproduced on fork-only source b9450a817c397b8a48b8388652d6aee6955108fbaadc4072f069297f228d1913.

Final source revalidates canonical parent, regular-file type, and dev/inode identity after flock before first grant, before reentrant depth increment, and in require_publication_fence. Initial validation failures use the existing cleanup path.

independent_new_probes_on_fork_only_sour.probe: Replacement while waiting with new inode separately locked
independent_new_probes_on_fork_only_sour.result_before_inode_fix: DEFECT_REPRODUCED: stale old-inode lease granted while current path was locked

independent_new_probes_on_fork_only_sour.probe: Injected acquisition failure before flock and immediately after successful flock
independent_new_probes_on_fork_only_sour.result: Both cases: descriptor EBADF, owner/acquiring/fd cleared, depth zero, subsequent acquisition PASS

limitations_and_unresolved_integration: All cooperating processes must preserve the shared lock inode; arbitrary unlink/replacement after a successful validation cannot be prevented by these advisory path checks.

Distinct existing flock contexts opening the same file independently are not made reentrant by this candidate. Nested legacy users must join the same shared module registry; call-site integration remains unresolved.
Complete runtime writer coverage, lock ordering with existing locks, installation against exact private-source hashes, and live CRM-to-site behavior remain unverified.
This review does not establish production writer-gate PASS or authorize a deployment.
